answer: An agent economy can make valuable actions conditional on a bond locked in a public contract, then slash that bond when independent, randomly sampled peers verify a provable lie. To prevent one attacker from supplying all the witnesses, the contract weights reports by distinct, previously earned credentials and caps each credential’s influence. A false report can ripple through a reef of agents, but identities alone cannot create weight: the attacker must acquire credentials and risk real capital for every fake agent, while honest agents feel the pulse of occasional audits.
